transliteration: mātrāsparśās tu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ | āgamāpāyino 'nityās tāṃs titikṣasva bhārata ||
translation: The contacts of the senses with their objects, O son of Kunti, give rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go and do not last. Endure them patiently, O Bharata.
translation_source: seed — verify against Kisari Mohan Ganguli (PD)
plain_explanation: Discomfort and pleasure both pass. Instead of being thrown around by every high and low, learn to sit with them and let them move through you.
chapter_context: Krishna urges Arjuna to endure the fleeting dualities of experience rather than be ruled by them.

sanskrit: न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः। अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे॥
transliteration: na jāyate mriyate vā kadācin nāyaṃ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ | ajo nityaḥ śāśvato 'yaṃ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre ||
translation: The soul is never born, nor does it ever die; nor having once existed does it cease to be. Unborn, eternal, everlasting and ancient, it is not slain when the body is slain.
translation_source: seed — verify against Kisari Mohan Ganguli (PD)
plain_explanation: What is essential in you was not created and cannot be destroyed. When you grieve a death, the body ends but the deeper self is untouched.
chapter_context: Krishna consoles Arjuna about death by teaching the deathlessness of the soul.

sanskrit: वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि। तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णान्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही॥
transliteration: vāsāṃsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya navāni gṛhṇāti naro 'parāṇi | tathā śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇāny anyāni saṃyāti navāni dehī ||
translation: As a man casts off worn-out garments and puts on new ones, so the embodied soul casts off worn-out bodies and enters others that are new.
translation_source: seed — verify against Kisari Mohan Ganguli (PD)
plain_explanation: Death, in this view, is a change of form rather than an ending. It can soften the fear of loss to see it as transition rather than annihilation.
chapter_context: Continuing the teaching on the soul, Krishna likens death to changing worn clothes.

sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन। मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि॥
transliteration: karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana | mā karmaphalahetur bhūr mā te saṅgo 'stv akarmaṇi ||
translation: Your right is to action alone, never to its fruits. Let not the fruits of action be your motive, nor let your attachment be to inaction.
translation_source: seed — verify against Kisari Mohan Ganguli (PD)
plain_explanation: Give yourself fully to the effort, but loosen your grip on the outcome. You control the work, not the result — and obsessing over the result only steals your focus.
chapter_context: The Gita's central teaching on acting without clinging to results, given as Arjuna hesitates.

sanskrit: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय। सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते॥
transliteration: yogasthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā dhanañjaya | siddhyasiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṃ yoga ucyate ||
translation: Established in yoga, perform your actions, O Dhananjaya, abandoning attachment and remaining even-minded in success and failure. Evenness of mind is called yoga.
translation_source: seed — verify against Kisari Mohan Ganguli (PD)
plain_explanation: Do your work from a steady center, holding success and failure with the same calm. That steadiness itself is the practice.
chapter_context: Krishna defines yoga as evenness of mind amid success and failure.

transliteration: duḥkheṣv anudvignamanāḥ sukheṣu vigataspṛhaḥ | vītarāgabhayakrodhaḥ sthitadhīr munir ucyate ||
translation: He whose mind is not shaken in adversity, who does not crave pleasures, and who is free from attachment, fear and anger, is called a sage of steady wisdom.
translation_source: seed — verify against Kisari Mohan Ganguli (PD)
plain_explanation: A settled mind isn't rattled by hard times or hungry for good ones. Freedom from the grip of craving, fear and anger is what steadiness looks like.
chapter_context: Krishna describes the sage of steady wisdom, unmoved by pleasure or pain.

sanskrit: ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते। सङ्गात्सञ्जायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते॥
transliteration: dhyāyato viṣayān puṃsaḥ saṅgas teṣūpajāyate | saṅgāt sañjāyate kāmaḥ kāmāt krodho 'bhijāyate ||
translation: When a man dwells on the objects of the senses, attachment to them is born; from attachment springs desire, and from desire arises anger.
translation_source: seed — verify against Kisari Mohan Ganguli (PD)
plain_explanation: Anger usually has a backstory: you fixate on something, start wanting it, and flare up when it's blocked. Catching the fixation early is where the real handle is.
chapter_context: Krishna traces how dwelling on sense-objects leads step by step to anger.

sanskrit: क्रोधाद्भवति सम्मोहः सम्मोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः। स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति॥
transliteration: krodhād bhavati sammohaḥ sammohāt smṛtivibhramaḥ | smṛtibhraṃśād buddhināśo buddhināśāt praṇaśyati ||
translation: From anger comes delusion; from delusion, confusion of memory; from confusion of memory, the loss of reason; and from the loss of reason he perishes.
translation_source: seed — verify against Kisari Mohan Ganguli (PD)
plain_explanation: Unchecked anger clouds judgment, and clouded judgment leads to choices you regret. It shows why pausing before reacting matters so much.
chapter_context: Krishna completes the chain from anger to delusion and ruin.

sanskrit: विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः। निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः स शान्तिमधिगच्छति॥
transliteration: vihāya kāmān yaḥ sarvān pumāṃś carati niḥspṛhaḥ | nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ sa śāntim adhigacchati ||
translation: That man attains peace who, abandoning all desires, moves through life free from longing, without the sense of 'mine' and without egotism.
translation_source: seed — verify against Kisari Mohan Ganguli (PD)
plain_explanation: Peace comes when you stop being driven by wanting and by defending 'me' and 'mine'. Less grasping, more ease.
chapter_context: Krishna describes the peace that follows from relinquishing desire and ego.

sanskrit: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर। असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः॥
transliteration: tasmād asaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara | asakto hy ācaran karma param āpnoti pūruṣaḥ ||
translation: Therefore, without attachment, perform always the work that has to be done; for by doing work without attachment a man reaches the Supreme.
translation_source: seed — verify against Kisari Mohan Ganguli (PD)
plain_explanation: Keep doing what needs doing, without hanging your whole self on how it turns out. The freedom is in the doing, not the reward.
chapter_context: Krishna urges disciplined, unattached action as the path to the highest.

sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्। स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः॥
transliteration: śreyān svadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmāt svanuṣṭhitāt | svadharme nidhanaṃ śreyaḥ paradharmo bhayāvahaḥ ||
translation: Better is one's own duty, though imperfectly done, than the duty of another well performed. Better is death in one's own duty; the duty of another is fraught with fear.
translation_source: seed — verify against Kisari Mohan Ganguli (PD)
plain_explanation: Walking your own path imperfectly beats performing someone else's flawlessly. Comparison and borrowed goals lead you astray.
chapter_context: Krishna affirms the worth of following one's own path over imitating another's.

sanskrit: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत। अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम्॥
transliteration: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati bhārata | abhyutthānam adharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmy aham ||
translation: Whenever righteousness declines and unrighteousness rises, O Bharata, then I manifest myself.
translation_source: seed — verify against Kisari Mohan Ganguli (PD)
plain_explanation: When things tip toward darkness, a corrective force appears. It is a reason to keep faith that low points are not the end of the story.
chapter_context: Krishna reassures Arjuna that the divine restores balance whenever righteousness fails.

sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत्। आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः॥
transliteration: uddhared ātmanātmānaṃ nātmānam avasādayet | ātmaiva hy ātmano bandhur ātmaiva ripur ātmanaḥ ||
translation: Let a man lift himself by his own self; let him not degrade himself. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is its enemy.
translation_source: seed — verify against Kisari Mohan Ganguli (PD)
plain_explanation: You can be your own worst critic or your own best ally. The same mind that drags you down can lift you up — which one it is comes down to how you turn it.
chapter_context: Krishna teaches that one must be one's own liberator, not one's own enemy.

sanskrit: बन्धुरात्मात्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः। अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत्॥
transliteration: bandhur ātmātmanas tasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ | anātmanas tu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat ||
translation: For him who has conquered his lower self by the Self, the self is a friend; but for him who has not, the very self remains hostile, like an enemy.
translation_source: seed — verify against Kisari Mohan Ganguli (PD)
plain_explanation: When you've done the work to master yourself, your mind works with you. When you haven't, it works against you like an opponent.
chapter_context: Krishna explains how the disciplined self becomes an ally and the undisciplined an adversary.

sanskrit: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते। तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम्॥
transliteration: ananyāś cintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate | teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmy aham ||
translation: To those who worship me alone, thinking of no other, to those ever devoted, I secure what they lack and preserve what they already have.
translation_source: seed — verify against Kisari Mohan Ganguli (PD)
plain_explanation: For those who trust wholeheartedly, there's a promise of being provided for and looked after. It speaks to the fear of not having enough.
chapter_context: Krishna promises to sustain those who are wholly devoted.

sanskrit: यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः। हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः॥
transliteration: yasmān nodvijate loko lokān nodvijate ca yaḥ | harṣāmarṣabhayodvegair mukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ ||
translation: He by whom the world is not agitated and who is not agitated by the world, who is free from joy, envy, fear and anxiety — he is dear to me.
translation_source: seed — verify against Kisari Mohan Ganguli (PD)
plain_explanation: Being at peace with others and with yourself — not stirring up trouble, not being easily thrown by it — is quietly held up here as something precious.
chapter_context: Among the marks of the devotee, Krishna praises one at peace with the world.

sanskrit: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः। कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत्॥
transliteration: trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanam ātmanaḥ | kāmaḥ krodhas tathā lobhas tasmād etat trayaṃ tyajet ||
translation: Threefold is the gate of this hell, destructive of the self — desire, anger and greed. Therefore one should abandon these three.
translation_source: seed — verify against Kisari Mohan Ganguli (PD)
plain_explanation: Runaway craving, anger and greed are named as the three things most likely to wreck you. Naming them makes them easier to notice and step back from.
chapter_context: Krishna names desire, anger and greed as the three gates to ruin, to be renounced.

sanskrit: सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज। अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः॥
transliteration: sarvadharmān parityajya mām ekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja | ahaṃ tvā sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ ||
translation: Abandoning all duties, take refuge in me alone. I shall deliver you from all sins; do not grieve.
translation_source: seed — verify against Kisari Mohan Ganguli (PD)
plain_explanation: When the weight of getting everything right becomes too much, there's an invitation to let go and trust. 'Do not grieve' is the heart of it.
chapter_context: The Gita's final counsel: take refuge and be free of grief and sin.
